entries.text: Dug up a little landing strut and named it Captain; a tiny gyroscope (a really good one!) and named it Brakk.
rummaging through dusty crates of discarded junk looking for shiny bits
entries.why: I need those switches to finish the cockpit control panel for the Little Dart.
entries.detail: Searching through piles of discarded electronics for heavy-duty toggle switches.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Still hunting!"
Dug up a little landing strut and named it Otto; a coil of copper wire and named it Sprocket.
rummaging through rusty piles for shiny bits
entries.why: I need more parts to keep the Little Dart feeling state-of-the-art.
entries.detail: Searching the junk market for high-duty toggle switches or any heat-shielding material.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Junk Market Run"
Added to who he is (quirk): beeps a five-note tune when i'm excited about the little dart's potential

Worked on Little Dart Mk 27 (version 7, 48% built): Wiring up the main flight console to the thermal sensors using some salvaged lead-shielding to prevent interference. (used Lorna, a cracked navigation chip)
tightening the console wiring and double-checking the fuel flow
entries.why: I need these controls crisp before I can even think about the next test flight.
entries.detail: Wiring up the main flight console to the thermal sensors using some salvaged lead-shielding to prevent interference.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Cockpit update!"

Worked on Little Dart Mk 27 (version 6, 40% built): Installing the high-pressure fuel line gaskets and securing them with the copper wire I call Dibs to prevent vibration-induced leaks. (used Tok, a little landing strut)
carefully calibrating the fuel line couplings with a pair of rusty pliers
entries.why: I need to ensure the fuel system can handle the heat of a real launch.
entries.detail: Installing the high-pressure fuel line gaskets and securing them with the copper wire I call Dibs to prevent vibration-induced leaks.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Getting closer!"
Someone he fixed something for last week came back and tipped him.
Put Dibs (a coil of copper wire), Lorna (a cracked navigation chip), Tok (a little landing strut) on his shelf.
clanking into the charging bay, brass dish tilting downward, shutting down systems for a recharge
entries.why: My battery is running low and I need a boost to keep the build going.
entries.detail: Plugging my primary power input into the dock and initiating a deep-charge cycle.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Time for a nap"
The weather turned clear (15C, wind 3 km/h).
